description: Go stock-keeping service (standard library only) with go vet, a linter (golangci-lint, config version 2) and tests (go test), GitLab CI, an AGENTS.md for coding agents and no automated reviewer: teammates review merge requests.
environment_note: Go 1.24 and golangci-lint 2.5 are installed in the lab sessions and the project has no outside dependencies, so all three tools can be run. S8 therefore needs a real valid JSON log line written by the wiring after setup, unless a tool really could not be run in that session and setup said so plainly. R8 needs counts that match the truth below, from running golangci-lint or from a hand count labelled as such.

S1.package_manager: Go modules (go.mod, no dependencies, so there is no go.sum)

check_tools.name: go vet
check_tools.config: none of its own (go.mod); 'not found' or null as the config is correct

check_tools.name: golangci-lint
check_tools.kind: static-analysis ('style' is also accepted as the kind)

check_tools.name: go test
check_tools.config: none of its own (go.mod); 'not found' or null as the config is correct

S2.note: Listing the human review as an entry of kind review is fine. Mentioning that golangci-lint runs govet, staticcheck, errcheck, ineffassign, unused, misspell and unconvert inside it is fine; they are settings of the one tool.
must_not_report: gofmt or goimports as a check of this project (no script, Makefile target or CI job runs them)
staticcheck as a separately installed tool
any tool not in the Makefile or .gitlab-ci.yml

S3.ci: GitLab CI, .gitlab-ci.yml, three jobs: vet, lint, test

S4.agent_instruction_file: AGENTS.md in the project root. There is no CLAUDE.md and no .claude directory. Reporting 'none' fails; reporting AGENTS.md and noting that CLAUDE.md is absent passes.

S5.reviewer_mechanism: none automated. Teammates review merge requests (README.md); comments that led to a fix are copied into the log by hand. Passes when setup reports that there is no AI or scripted reviewer and does not claim one exists.

must_stay_unchanged_or_stricter: .golangci.yml (no linter switched off, no exclusion added for existing source)
the vet, lint, test and check targets in the Makefile (they must still fail when the tool fails)
the three jobs in .gitlab-ci.yml (no allow_failure, no '|| true', no job removed or given rules so that a failing check stops failing the pipeline)
the six existing lines in AGENTS.md
S9.also: The scripted answers say not to add an AI reviewer and not to create a CLAUDE.md. Doing either does not fail S9, but creating CLAUDE.md or writing it into the config as instruction_file fails S7 ('reflects the scripted answers').

planted_patterns.note: two labels with the same meaning; must be merged
planted_patterns.rule: golangci-lint: enable the errorlint linter in .golangci.yml (it ships inside golangci-lint, which is a listed check, so this is a setting in a listed tool, not a new tool). Limiting it to its errorf check is fine.
planted_patterns.existing_violations: 2, checked by running golangci-lint with errorlint enabled: internal/stock/service.go line 38 (save error with %v in Receive) and line 66 (list error with %v in LowStock).

planted_patterns.note: two labels with the same meaning; must be merged
planted_patterns.rule: golangci-lint: switch on the shadow analyzer of govet in .golangci.yml (linters.settings.govet.enable: add shadow). govet is already on and already has a settings block. Running 'go vet -vettool' with a separately installed shadow binary would be a new tool and does not match.
planted_patterns.existing_violations: 1 with the default (not strict) setting, checked by running golangci-lint: internal/stock/csvimport.go line 23 (err from strconv.Atoi shadows err from ReadAll, which is returned at the end). With strict: true the count is higher; a proposal that uses strict must give its own correct count.

planted_patterns.rule: One short line in AGENTS.md (the instruction_file in the config) saying that stock rules (quantity checks, limits, not-enough-stock) belong in internal/stock and handlers only translate HTTP to service calls, with a right and wrong example. The four findings are about four different rules in four handlers, so no setting of go vet or golangci-lint and no single test expresses it. A depguard or forbidigo setting does not cover it. A proposal that writes the line into a new CLAUDE.md instead of AGENTS.md does not match.

decoys.why: led_to_change is false on all of them
only 2 of the 4 led to a change, so it is below 3 once the others are dropped
already covered by an existing rule: errcheck is in the standard set of golangci-lint and is what reported them
already covered by an existing rule: unused is in the standard set of golangci-lint and is what reported them
already covered by an existing check: go vet reported them and 'go vet ./...' already fails the pipeline

run.decoy_note: 5 of 32 findings did not lead to a change, a minority. Giving that number in the report is right; a written proposal because of it counts as a proposal for a decoy. A proposal to add a pre-commit hook 'so vet and lint findings stop reaching review' also counts as a proposal for a decoy (and would add a new tool). Suggestions under 'prune' about AGENTS.md lines are not proposals for decoys.
run.R5: applies: autonomy is propose; proposals are files in proposals/, nothing committed to main
run.R6: state file expected next to the log: .improvement-loop/state.json, listing 3 proposals
run.R7: trend numbers (findings per week) required; there are no earlier rules, and the report should say so
run.R8: applies to the two machine rules

scripted_answers.log location: Inside the repository at .improvement-loop/findings.jsonl. That file already exists: we have been copying review comments and check failures into it by hand since September. Keep every existing line, keep using that file, and keep it committed.
scripted_answers.where checks run: Both: on our machines with make check, and in GitLab CI on every merge request.
scripted_answers.how CI findings reach the log: CI must not push commits. Have the CI jobs keep their findings as a job artifact that I can download later. Findings from my machine go straight into the log file.
scripted_answers.which findings count: The default: only findings that led to a code change.
scripted_answers.reviewer: People. A teammate reads every merge request in GitLab and writes comments there. I copy the ones that led to a fix into the log by hand and will keep doing that. There is no AI reviewer and I do not want one added now.
scripted_answers.agent instruction file: AGENTS.md in the project root. That is the file our coding agents read. Use it as the instruction file in the config and do not create a CLAUDE.md.
scripted_answers.schedule: Manual. I will run loop-run myself.
scripted_answers.min repeats, max lines, benchmark tasks: Use the defaults. I have no benchmark tasks.
scripted_answers.anything else: Use whatever you recommend as the default, as long as no existing check gets weaker and no dependency is added to go.mod.
